name: Dharmasthala Shri Manjunatha Swamy Temple
hook: A Shiva temple run by a Jain family that feeds thousands daily.
why: Gates open at 4 am, and by noon the queue complex is a slow river of devotees shuffling toward Manjunatha. Then you walk across to Annapoorna, a kitchen built to feed 30,000 to 70,000 people a day, and eat a free meal on the floor beside strangers. Few places show Tulunadu's mix of Shaiva worship and Jain stewardship this plainly.

train.notes: No railway station near Dharmasthala in the sources checked; ride or take a bus.

bestTime: Weekday mornings, right at 6:30 am darshan, or the 5 pm evening session. Avoid weekends and festival days if you hate queues.
decJanNote: Dry roads and cool mornings make this an easy day ride. Weekend queues can run long, so go midweek. The temple says darshan, meals and rooms may vary on crowded days. Check the official site for festival dates in this window before you go.
vegFoodNearby: Annapoorna dining hall (temple annadana, free veg meal, inside the temple complex): lunch 11 am–2:30 pm, dinner 7–10 pm

temple.dressCode: Men must remove shirt and vest before entering the sanctum. Men in half-pants and women in nighties are not allowed in for darshan. No bags inside, no mobile phone use in the temple, children under 2 not allowed in the sanctum.
temple.darshanTimings: 6:30 am–2:30 pm (darshan pauses around 12:00–12:15 pm for Mahapooja and Nithyabali; the afternoon line closes at 2:30 pm or when the queue ends) and 5:00–8:30 pm. Gates open 4 am. Timings may change on special days.
temple.annadana: Free meals at Annapoorna dining hall, 11 am–2:30 pm and 7–10 pm. Annadana begins after Maha Naivedya (11:30 am). Breakfast is served in the queue line on crowded days.

bikeTips: About 97 km via Karkala and Belthangady, roughly 1h 50m. Park only in the allotted parking slots (temple rule). Leave the riding jacket and bag with the bike or at your room: bags are not allowed inside.
safety: Heavy crowds on weekends and festival days; keep valuables close, as the temple itself warns. Use the police-aid posts if you get separated from your group. Do not ride back late at night on the Belthangady–Karkala stretch if tired.

name: Ratnagiri Bahubali, Manjusha Museum & Vintage Car Museum, Dharmasthala
hook: A 39-foot Bahubali, old cameras, and Gandhi's car in one afternoon.
why: The 39-foot monolithic Bahubali on Ratnagiri hill was dragged 64 km from Karkala on a 64-wheel trolley in 1970, and installed in 1982. Twenty minutes of steps gets you a view over the whole temple town. Down below, Manjusha is a magpie's dream of coastal heirlooms, cameras and nutcrackers, and the car museum keeps every vehicle in running order, including one Gandhi travelled in.
bestTime: Bahubali hill in the morning (the temple itself recommends mornings to dodge heat and humidity); museums before or after the noon darshan break.
decJanNote: Clear winter air means the best views from Ratnagiri all year. Pair it with Manjunatha darshan and lunch at Annapoorna.
vegFoodNearby: Annapoorna dining hall (temple annadana, free veg meal, about 1 km away): lunch 11 am–2:30 pm, dinner 7–10 pm
bikeTips: The statue is about 1 km from the Manjunatha temple, by steps (around 20 minutes) or by road. Opening hours from the official site: Bahubali hill 7 am–6:30 pm; Manjusha Museum 9:30 am–5:30 pm; Vintage Car Museum 8:30 am–1 pm and 2–7 pm.
safety: Midday sun on the open hilltop is harsh; there are shelters and drinking water at the top. Steps can be crowded on holidays.

name: Sowthadka Shri Mahaganapati Temple
hook: Ganapati under the open sky, no walls, no roof.
why: Legend says Ganapati asked the farmers not to build him a temple so nobody would ever face restrictions here. So the idol sits out in a meadow, open to the sky and hung with bells offered by devotees whose wishes came true. Come for the appa prasada and keep an eye on the monkeys.
bestTime: Morning, pairing it with Dharmasthala (about 16 km away).
decJanNote: An easy add-on to a Dharmasthala day. The official Dharmasthala site lists it among nearby places. Sources say the temple's annual Mahapuja is in January, so expect bigger crowds then.
vegFoodNearby: Temple prasada meal (served to devotees, per the Dharmasthala official site; timing not confirmed, verify locally)
Appa and laddu prasada sold at temple counters

temple.dressCode: Not confirmed online. Yatradham suggests traditional or formal clothes. Verify locally.
temple.darshanTimings: Not confirmed online; sources conflict. The idol is open-air and described as open round the clock, while listed timings range from about 5–6 am to 7:30–10 pm. Verify locally.
temple.annadana: The temple serves a prasada meal to devotees (Dharmasthala official site). Timing not confirmed online; verify locally.

bikeTips: About 3 km from Kokkada, off the Dharmasthala–Kukke road (SH37); entrance arch is on the highway. Around 16 km from Dharmasthala, so do both in one ride.
safety: Monkeys around the shrine snatch food and prasada; keep bags zipped. The highway stretch near Kokkada carries pilgrim buses.

name: Kukke Shri Subrahmanya Temple
hook: The serpent god's seat, with Kumara Parvatha looming overhead.
why: Kukke sits on the Kumaradhara river with Kumara Parvatha rising behind it, and it is where Karnataka comes for naga rituals like Ashlesha Bali and Sarpa Samskara. Men strip to the waist in the darshan line, priests chant through Ashlesha Bali shifts, and the free annadana keeps going through lunch and dinner. It's also the base camp for the state's most famous trek.

train.notes: Subrahmanya Road station is about 12 km from the temple (Karnataka Tourism). It is not on the Konkan line, so from Udupi you would change at Mangaluru. Train times not checked; verify locally.

bestTime: Weekday mornings. Saturdays, Sundays and November–December festival days are very crowded.
decJanNote: Cool and dry, but this is festival season at Kukke, and sources flag heavy crowds on November–December festival days. Go midweek, stay the night, and check seva schedules before booking Ashlesha Bali or Sarpa Samskara.
vegFoodNearby: Temple annadana (free veg meals, inside the temple complex): lunch from 11:30 am to 2 pm, dinner 7:30–9:30 pm

temple.dressCode: Men remove shirt and vest before joining the darshan line; dhoti or white pancha for sevas such as Ashlesha Bali and Sarpa Samskara. Women: saree, churidar or salwar with dupatta, or other modest wear. Shorts and sleeveless tops are not appropriate.
temple.darshanTimings: Sources differ. Commonly listed as about 6:30 am–1:30 pm and 3:30–8:00/9:00 pm, closed roughly 1:30–3:30 pm. Timings change on special occasions; verify locally.
temple.annadana: Free lunch 11:30 am–2 pm and free dinner 7:30–9:30 pm (two non-official sources agree); hours may shift on festival days. Sarpa Samskara is a two-day seva: register in advance and attend both days with photo ID.

bikeTips: About 164 km, roughly 2h 45m. The last stretch from Dharmasthala via Kokkada (SH37) passes Sowthadka. Stay the night if you're doing a seva or the trek.
safety: Huge crowds on weekends and festival days. Don't swim in the Kumaradhara when the current is strong. The approach roads are forest roads, so avoid riding after dark.

name: Kumara Parvatha Trek (Kukke Subramanya route)
hook: One of Karnataka's toughest treks, now permit-only and no camping.
why: From Kukke the trail climbs out of the Kumaradhara valley through forest and grassland to a 1,712 m summit. Old trip reports describe it as a two-day epic with a night at Bhattara Mane, but that's gone. It's now a single, brutal day, booked online, with a strict exit time. If the Kukke side stays shut, the Beedahalli route from the Kodagu side is the shorter way up.

train.notes: About 12 km from Kukke (Karnataka Tourism); not on the Konkan line, change at Mangaluru. You'd need the night before in Kukke to make an early start.

bestTime: October–November post-monsoon; the trek is closed in the monsoon and in summer fire season.
decJanNote: The trek reopened on 18 Oct 2026, but only on the Beedahalli–Kumara Parvatha–Beedahalli route. Daijiworld (17 Oct) and Elneeru (updated 31 Oct) both say the Kukke route had no reopening date. Check Aranya Vihaara before planning. If Kukke is still unlisted, book Beedahalli instead (about 208 km from Manipal, 7 km each way).
vegFoodNearby: Kukke temple annadana (free veg meals): lunch 11:30 am–2 pm, dinner 7:30–9:30 pm

trek.duration: Kukke round trip about 20–22 km, roughly 11–12 hours, in a single day. Beedahalli round trip about 14 km, 7–8 hours. Kukke side: 5:30 am start and 6 pm exit were reported for last season; this season's times are not confirmed.
trek.howToBook: Online only via the Karnataka Forest Dept Aranya Vihaara portal (aranyavihaara.karnataka.gov.in). Book 1–30 days ahead. Carry the original ID used to book. Cancellations 8+ days out get a 50% refund, within 7 days nothing (rules effective 15 Jul 2026). Daily cap: 150/day for Kukke (minister, Mar 2026). Portal showed 300 slots/day for Beedahalli in Nov 2026. Fee about ₹350 reported in Dec 2025; confirm on portal. No overnight stay or camping, including at Bhattara Mane/Girigadde. Plastic and paper banned.

bikeTips: Distance is to Kukke Subramanya (trailhead side). The Beedahalli checkpost (Kodagu side) is about 208 km, 3h 40m from Manipal. Sleep in Kukke the night before; you need to be at the gate before dawn. Don't plan to ride back the same evening after a 12-hour trek.
safety: Overnight stays and camping inside the sanctuary are banned; plan to be out by the exit time. Long, steep, exposed sections, so carry 3+ litres of water and food in steel containers. Plastic and paper are banned. Bhattara Mane meal service is not confirmed for 2026, so don't count on it. Leeches in the lower forest early in the season. Don't trek alone, and don't attempt it without a valid permit.

name: Gadaikallu (Jamalabad Fort)
hook: Tipu's rock fortress, reached by 1,876 steps cut into granite.
why: Gadaikallu is a bald granite thumb you can see from the Belthangady road. Tipu Sultan fortified it in 1794 and named it after his mother; the British took it five years later. The 1,876 rock-cut steps get narrow and steep near the top, and the reward is the whole Charmadi ridge laid out like a map.
bestTime: Start right at opening (gate around 6–7:30 am) to climb before the rock heats up.
decJanNote: This is the season for it. Karnataka Tourism says entry is allowed only October to May, because the rock is lethal in the rain. Winter mornings are cooler, and the steps should have dried out by December.

trek.duration: 1,876 steps. Allow 1.5–2 hours up and about the same down. Entry window 6 am–4 pm (Wikipedia, karnataka.com); one 2021 visitor found the gate opening around 7–7:30 am.
trek.howToBook: Entry ticket at the forest check post at the base. Fee reported as ₹40 (karnataka.com) to ₹50 (2021 blog); confirm at the gate. Whether it now needs Aranya Vihaara online booking is unconfirmed; verify locally before riding out.

bikeTips: About 88 km via Karkala–Belthangady; the fort is around 8 km north of Belthangady off the road toward Ujire/Charmadi. Combine with Dharmasthala (about 15 km away) or Venur on the same day.
safety: Steep, exposed rock-cut steps with sheer drops near the summit; they're slippery when wet, which is why entry is closed in the monsoon. Overnight stays are prohibited, so come down before closing. No drinking water at the top; carry plenty.

name: Bandaje Falls Trek via Ballalarayana Durga
hook: Fort ruins, endless grass ridges, then a 200-foot drop.
why: You start at a village temple in Durgadahalli, climb through forest to the crumbling walls of Ballalarayana Durga, then roll across grass ridges until the land falls away at Bandaje. The falls drop about 200 feet into the Belthangady side. The walk back up is the part everyone underestimates.
bestTime: October to early December for water in the falls; start 6–6:30 am.
decJanNote: The grass ridges and fort views are great in December. The falls are another story: Explurger says they shrink to a trickle by December–February. Go early in the window if the waterfall matters. Both treks were open and bookable as of Nov 2026.

trek.duration: From Durgadahalli: 3 km (about 1.5 h) to Ballalarayana Durga, then 3.5 km (about 2.5 h) to the falls. Around 13–15 km and 7–8 hours round trip.
trek.howToBook: Aranya Vihaara portal (aranyavihaara.karnataka.gov.in), Chikkamagaluru district. 'Bandaje Falls' and 'Ballalarayana Durga' are listed as separate treks, each with 300 slots/day (Elneeru snapshot, 4 Nov 2026). Fee reported as ₹500 (Bengaluru Trekkers, Nov 2026); older sources say ₹250, so confirm on the portal. 'Bandaje Trek via Volambra' from the Belthangady side was listed closed. Carry the ID used to book.

bikeTips: Routed to Sunkasale, the village nearest the Durgadahalli trailhead (Kalabhyraveshwara temple), about 128 km via Charmadi Ghat, so you climb the ghat before dawn. Sources say jeeps can go about 1 km past the temple and other vehicles should park at it. Leave Manipal very early, or stay at a Sunkasale/Durgadahalli homestay the night before.
safety: Easy to lose the trail in the grasslands, so Karnataka Tourism advises an authorised guide. Loose gravel on the descent and a long climb back past the fort. No shops or water on the trail: carry 2+ litres and food. Single-use plastic is fined at checkposts. Take care at the Rani Jhari cliff edge. The Belthangady/Volambra approach was listed closed, so don't try it without a permit. Ride Charmadi Ghat in daylight only.

name: Ermai (Ermayi) Falls, Malavanthige
hook: A forest waterfall whose main path may still be closed to visitors.
why: Ermai sits in the Kudremukh buffer forest above Belthangady, reached on a rough last kilometre that ends at a riverside clearing. When it was open, people walked a boulder-strewn stream and crossed a wobbly bamboo bridge to reach it. In 2021 a blogger found the landowner had closed the path to the main falls, and nothing since confirms it reopened.
bestTime: Just after the monsoon (Oct–Nov), if access is open.
decJanNote: Two strikes. Access to the main falls was blocked by the private landowner (2021 report), and Trip.com still lists it as closed. In a December visit the water was not even knee-deep. Pick Bandaje or Gadaikallu instead unless locals confirm it's open.
bikeTips: Coordinates and distance are for Kajuru village on the Didupe road in Belthangady taluk, the approach area. The falls' own location wasn't geocodable; sources place it about 5 km from Didupe and 18 km from Ujire, at Malavanthige. The last km is rough and hard on low-clearance vehicles.
safety: A 35-year-old filmmaker died here in May 2018 after slipping on wet rocks during heavy rain. Don't climb the rocks around the falls, and don't swim. The bamboo bridge sways badly, so cross one at a time. Respect private-property closures and any forest department boards.

name: Charmadi Ghat Ride (Ujire to Kottigehara)
hook: Twelve hairpins from the paddy plains to the coffee country.
why: The road climbs from Charmadi village at about 150 m to Kottigehara at about 970 m in a tight string of 12 hairpins. On a clear day you can see the Mangaluru coastline from the top, and Gadaikallu and Bandaje's ridges line up on the way. It's the classic Manipal ride for anyone who measures a weekend in corners.
bestTime: Early morning on a weekday, in daylight only.
decJanNote: Dry winter tarmac is the best of the year; the closures in the sources are all monsoon landslides. Mornings can be misty near the top, so wait for it to lift. No current ban was found in the sources checked, but check local news before you go.
bikeTips: Distance is to Charmadi village at the foot of the ghat (via Karkala–Belthangady–Ujire). The climb to Kottigehara at the top adds about 24 km (Kottigehara is 127 km, 2h 10m from Manipal). Fuel up in Ujire or Belthangady. Continue to Mudigere and Belur for the long ride, or loop back via Dharmasthala.
safety: 12 hairpins on a narrow road. Buses and lorries cut corners, so stay left and never overtake blind. Landslides hit regularly in the monsoon: a hill collapsed at the 10th turn in July 2024. Past orders have banned heavy vehicles (2018) and all night traffic, with light vehicles allowed only 6 am–7 pm (2021). When Shiradi Ghat shuts, as in June 2025, traffic is diverted here and jams build. Don't ride the ghat at night. In mist, use low beam and slow right down.

name: Coorg Long Ride via Sullia: Madikeri, Abbey Falls & Dubare
hook: Coast to coffee hills in one long, winding day.
why: The road leaves the coast, runs inland through Sullia and climbs into Kodagu's coffee shade to Madikeri. Abbey Falls is a short hop from town, tumbling through private coffee and spice estates, with a hanging bridge facing it. Next morning, push east to Dubare on the Kaveri, where the Jungle Lodges elephant camp sits on the riverbank.
bestTime: Two days minimum. Leave Manipal at first light, reach Madikeri by lunch, Abbey Falls in the afternoon, Dubare next morning.
decJanNote: Cool, dry Kodagu winter: crisp mornings and clear roads. Abbey Falls has less water than in the monsoon, but the road is the point. Add Talacauvery–Bhagamandala, about 48 km from Madikeri, for a temple morning.
bikeTips: OSRM route to Madikeri is about 194 km, roughly 3h 20m of riding, via Mangaluru–Sullia–Sampaje. Abbey Falls is about 6–8 km from Madikeri and open 9 am–5 pm. Dubare's elephant camp is near Kushalnagar on the Kaveri. Activity timings and fees were not found online; check with Jungle Lodges (info@junglelodges.com) before going.
safety: Sampaje ghat and the climb into Madikeri carry buses and trucks; don't ride the ghats after dark. Bathing or swimming at Abbey Falls is not allowed. Keep a respectful distance from the elephants at Dubare, and follow camp staff instructions.

name: Talacauvery & Bhagamandala (Triveni Sangama, Bhagandeshwara Temple)
hook: Where the Kaveri begins: a spring-fed tank high on Brahmagiri.
why: At Bhagamandala the Kaveri meets the Kannike and the unseen Sujyothi, and pilgrims bathe and perform rites for their ancestors at the Triveni Sangama beside the Bhagandeshwara temple. Eight kilometres uphill, at 1,276 m, Talacauvery's small kundike is held to be the river's source. Steps beside the shrine lead up Brahmagiri to a 360-degree view across the hills.
bestTime: Early morning, as part of a Coorg overnight. Tula Sankramana (mid-October) is the big festival day, outside this travel window.
decJanNote: Clear winter skies give the best Brahmagiri views, and there's no October festival crush. It's a long day on its own, so fold it into the Coorg long ride with a night in Madikeri.

temple.dressCode: Not confirmed online; dress traditionally and expect to remove footwear. Verify locally.

bikeTips: Bhagamandala is about 191 km (3h 40m) from Manipal and about 33 km from Madikeri; Talacauvery is about 8 km further uphill. Do the Sangama first, then ride up.
safety: Narrow, steep hill road up to Talacauvery, often misty; ride slowly and not after dark. Hold railings on the Brahmagiri steps on windy days. Take care bathing at the Sangama, where river levels change.

name: Belur Chennakeshava & Halebidu Hoysaleswara Temples
hook: Soapstone carved so fine it looks like lace.
why: In 2023 UNESCO listed the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas, and these are two of the three temples. King Vishnuvardhana consecrated Belur's Chennakeshava in 1117, and it is still a working Vaishnava temple, with bracket maidens on pillar tops and a Narasimha pillar carved down to a tiny bull. Sixteen kilometres on, Halebidu's twin-shrined Hoysaleswara wraps about 340 large reliefs and friezes of the epics around its walls.

train.notes: Nearest railhead is Hassan junction, about 40 km from Belur (Karnataka Tourism). Not a sensible approach from Udupi.

bestTime: Belur at opening (7:30 am) for soft light on the carvings; Halebidu late morning.
decJanNote: Ideal winter ride: up Charmadi Ghat at dawn, through Mudigere coffee country, Belur by mid-morning. Stay overnight in Belur or Hassan rather than riding the ghat back in the dark.

temple.dressCode: Not confirmed online. Belur is an active temple, so dress modestly. Verify locally.
temple.darshanTimings: Belur Chennakeshava: 7:30 am–7:30 pm daily (Karnataka Tourism). Halebidu Hoysaleswara: not confirmed online, verify locally.

bikeTips: OSRM gives Belur at about 175 km, 2h 50m (Halebidu about 196 km, 3h 20m), routed over Charmadi Ghat. Belur to Halebidu is about 16 km. Make it an overnight: two ghat descents in one day is too much.
safety: This route crosses Charmadi Ghat, so read that entry: 12 hairpins, buses, and monsoon landslides. Ride the ghat in daylight only. Watch for cattle and speed breakers on the Mudigere–Belur rural roads.

name: Venur Bahubali
hook: A 38-foot Bahubali from 1604, standing quietly by the Phalguni.
why: Long before Dharmasthala's Bahubali, the Jain chief Timmanna Ajila raised this 38-foot monolith on the bank of the Phalguni in 1604. It sees a fraction of Dharmasthala's crowds, so you may get the whole lawn to yourself.
bestTime: Morning, on the way to Gadaikallu or Dharmasthala.
decJanNote: Dry, bright winter light on the granite, and it slots neatly into a Gadaikallu or Dharmasthala ride.
bikeTips: About 70 km via Karkala. Venur is on the Karkala/Moodbidri–Dharmasthala side roads. Opening hours weren't found online; verify locally.
safety: Village roads with buses and school traffic; take it easy through Venur. Remove footwear where asked, and don't climb on the statue platform.

name: Shishila Shishileshwara Temple (Matsya Theertha)
hook: A Shiva temple whose river fish have been protected since 1930.
why: On the Kapila river at the foot of the Ghats, the Shishileshwara temple's pools hold shoals of fish that villagers treat as sacred and feed with beaten and puffed rice. A British collector banned fishing here in 1930. After poachers poisoned the river in 1996, villagers put up a memorial stone and formed a group to guard the fish.
bestTime: Morning, after Dharmasthala or Sowthadka; Kokkada is the turn-off.
decJanNote: Lower winter water makes the fish easier to see in the clear pools. Combine with Sowthadka (via Kokkada) and Dharmasthala.
bikeTips: About 121 km. Wikipedia notes buses from Dharmasthala or Uppinangady stop near the temple, or reach Kokkada and take a jeep or auto. On a bike, ride via Kokkada.
safety: Fishing is banned. Feed the fish only beaten rice or puffed rice, never packaged food. River-edge steps get slippery; don't wade in.
